preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.strip()) <= 1000 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line.strip()) == t)
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, s in zip(test_cases_n, test_cases_s))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line is a string s of length n (1 ≤ n ≤ 40) consisting of lowercase English letters.

preconditions.expression: all(s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in test_cases_s)
preconditions.description: Each string s contains only lowercase letters of the English alphabet.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i].isdigit() and 0 <= int(output_lines[i]) <= n for i, n in enumerate(test_cases_n))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is an integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ n) representing the minimum number of characters to permute to sort the string.

postconditions.expression: all((''.join(sorted(s)) == sorted(s) or any(k == len(set(s)) for k in range(0, n+1) if can_sort_with_k(s, k))) for s, n in zip(test_cases_s, test_cases_n))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output k is the smallest integer such that selecting k characters of s and permuting them can result in the string being sorted alphabetically. The helper can_sort_with_k(s, k) is true if there exists a subset of k characters in s that can be permuted to make the entire string sorted.
